coverageNotes: Introductory recognition of compound-index range construction. Boundary and order distractors additionally test general semantics. Does not establish production-scale performance, independent coding ability, or hard-model discrimination.

questions.concept: Constructing an equality-prefix range over a Convex compound index
questions.question: Which handler uses by_sensor_time to return only the specified sensor’s readings from startTime through endTime, including both endpoints, ordered oldest first?

options.text:
```ts
return await ctx.db
  .query("temperatures")
  .withIndex("by_sensor_time", (q) =>
    q
      .gte("timestamp", args.startTime)
      .lte("timestamp", args.endTime)
  )
  .filter((q) => q.eq(q.field("sensorId"), args.sensorId))
  .order("asc")
  .collect();
```
options.rationale: Moves the leading sensorId equality outside the index range into a later filter. The timestamp range therefore lacks its required leading index-field equality. Static diagnostics and actual runtime behavior are recorded separately in execution-evidence.json.

options.text:
```ts
return await ctx.db
  .query("temperatures")
  .withIndex("by_sensor_time", (q) =>
    q
      .eq("sensorId", args.sensorId)
      .gt("timestamp", args.startTime)
      .lte("timestamp", args.endTime)
  )
  .order("asc")
  .collect();
```
options.rationale: The strict lower bound excludes rows exactly at startTime. Other rows, the upper endpoint, and ordering remain correct.

options.text:
```ts
return await ctx.db
  .query("temperatures")
  .withIndex("by_sensor_time", (q) =>
    q
      .eq("sensorId", args.sensorId)
      .gte("timestamp", args.startTime)
      .lte("timestamp", args.endTime)
  )
  .order("asc")
  .collect();
```
options.rationale: Matches sensorId as the equality prefix, bounds timestamp inclusively, and traverses the compound index in ascending order.

options.text:
```ts
return await ctx.db
  .query("temperatures")
  .withIndex("by_sensor_time", (q) =>
    q
      .eq("sensorId", args.sensorId)
      .gte("timestamp", args.startTime)
      .lte("timestamp", args.endTime)
  )
  .order("desc")
  .collect();
```
options.rationale: Selects the correct rows but returns them newest first. It fails when the result contains different timestamps.
